conditions: Validity: The authorization and right vested by virtue of this action is valid for three (3) years from the effective date of the Motion. The Department of Building Inspection shall have issued a Building Permit or Site Permit to construct the project and/or commence the approved use within this three-year period. (standard)

Expiration and Renewal: Should a Building or Site Permit be sought after the three (3) year period has lapsed, the project sponsor must seek a renewal of this Authorization by filing an application for an amendment to the original Authorization or a new application for Authorization. Should the project sponsor decline to so file, and decline to withdraw the permit application, the Commission shall conduct a public hearing in order to consider the revocation of the Authorization. (standard)

Diligent Pursuit: Once a site or Building Permit has been issued, construction must commence within the timeframe required by the Department of Building Inspection and be continued diligently to completion. Failure to do so shall be grounds for the Commission to consider revoking the approval if more than three (3) years have passed since this Authorization was approved. (standard)

Extension: All time limits in the preceding three paragraphs may be extended at the discretion of the Zoning Administrator where implementation of the project is delayed by a public agency, an appeal or a legal challenge and only by the length of time for which such public agency, appeal or challenge has caused delay. (standard)

Conformity with Current Law: No application for Building Permit, Site Permit, or other entitlement shall be approved unless it complies with all applicable provisions of City Codes in effect at the time of such approval. (standard)

Garbage, Composting and Recycling Storage: Space for the collection and storage of garbage, composting, and recycling shall be provided within enclosed areas on the property and clearly labeled and illustrated on the building permit plans. Space for the collection and storage of recyclable and compostable materials that meets the size, location, accessibility and other standards specified by the San Francisco Recycling Program shall be provided at the ground level of the buildings. (standard)
Noise: P lans submitted with the building permit application for the approved project shall incorporate acoustical insulation and other sound proofing measures to control noise. (standard)

Enforcement: Violation of any of the Planning Department conditions of approval contained in this Motion or of any other provisions of Planning Code applicable to this Project shall be subject to the enforcement procedures and administrative penalties set forth under Planning Code Section 176 or Section 176.1. The Planning Department may also refer the violation complaints to other city departments and agencies for appropriate enforcement action under their jurisdiction. (standard)

Revocation due to Violation of Conditions: Should implementation of this Project result in complaints from interested property owners, residents, or commercial lessees which are not resolved by the Project Sponsor and found to be in violation of the Planning Code and/or the specific conditions of approval for the Project as set forth in Exhibit A of this Motion, the Zoning Administrator shall refer such complaints to the Commission, after which it may hold a public hearing on the matter to consider revocation of this authorization. Operation (standard)

Eating and Drinking Uses (A): The business operator shall maintain the main entrance to the building and all sidewalks abutting the subject property in a clean and sanitary condition in compliance with the Department of Public Works Street and Sidewalk Maintenance Standards. In addition, the operator shall be responsible for daily monitoring of the sidewalk within a one-block radius of the subject business to maintain the sidewalk free of paper or other litter associated with the business during business hours, in accordance with Article 1, Section 34 of the San Francisco Police Code. (standard)

Eating and Drinking Uses (B): When located within an enclosed space, the premises shall be adequately soundproofed or insulated for noise and operated so that incidental noise shall not be audible beyond the premises or in other sections of the building, and fixed -source equipment noise shall not exceed the decibel levels specified in the San Francisco Noise Control Ordinance. (standard)

Eating and Drinking Uses (C): While it is inevitable that some low level of odor may be detectable to nearby residents and passersby, appropriate odor control equipment shall be installed in conformance with the approved plans and maintained to prevent any significant noxious or offensive odors from escaping the premises. (standard)

Eating and Drinking Uses (D): Garbage, recycling, and compost containers shall be kept within the premises and hidden from public view, and placed outside only when being serviced by the disposal company. Trash shall be contained and disposed of pursuant to garbage and recycling receptacles guidelines set forth by the Department of Public Works. (standard)

Sidewalk Maintenance: The Project Sponsor shall maintain the main entrance to the building and all sidewalks abutting the subject property in a clean and sanitary condition in compliance with the Department of Public Works Streets and Sidewalk Maintenance Standards. (standard)

Community Liaison: Prior to issuance of a building permit to construct the project and implement the approved use, the Project Sponsor shall appoint a community liaison officer to deal with the issues of concern to owners and occupants of nearby properties. The Project Sponsor shall provide the Zoning Administrator and all registered neighborhood groups for the area with written notice of the name, business address, and telephone number of the community liaison. (standard)

Notices Posted at Bars and Entertainment Venues: Notices urging patrons to leave the establishment and neighborhood in a quiet, peaceful, and orderly fashion and to not litter or block driveways in the neighborhood, shall be well-lit and prominently displayed at all entrances to and exits from the establishment. (standard)
comparable_cases.why_comparable: Bar use (Type 48) in the CCB district at 690 Sacramento, 219 m away, filed June 2023 and approved November 2023. Same zoning district, same conditional-use pathway under Planning Code Section 810, recent decision establishes current Commission expectations.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Use decision: Bar CUA in CCB was approved with conditions in 5.5 months (171 days filing to decision). Standard conditions included noise control, community liaison officer, and patron notices at exits. No unusual restrictions on hours or operations, confirming the Commission approves bar uses in CCB when neighborhood impacts are managed.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: ABC Type 48 referral for the bar at 690 Sacramento (RM 212) approved in January 2024, following the November 2023 CUA. Shows the two-step process: CUA first, then ABC referral, and that Planning routinely approves the ABC application once the CUA is granted.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Agency referral: Planning approved the Type 48 ABC referral for 690 Sacramento after CUA 2023-005339CUA was granted, confirming the standard sequence: obtain CUA approval, then ABC applies the license. The referral approval took 204 days but was held pending the CUA decision; once the CUA was final the ABC referral was routine.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Board of Supervisors Public Convenience or Necessity referral for the same 690 Sacramento bar (Type 48), approved January 2024. Demonstrates that even a PCN finding from the Board of Supervisors was granted for a bar in the CCB district, supporting the conclusion that the district is not hostile to bar uses.

ABC Type 48 bar approval at 447 Bush Street, 230 m away in the C-3-R district, decided May 2022. Different zoning (C-3-R permits bars principally, CCB requires CU) but close proximity shows Planning's comfort with bar density in this downtown/Chinatown edge area.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Agency referral: Planning approved a Type 48 bar in the nearby C-3-R district in 7 days as principally permitted. While the C-3-R zoning differs from CCB, the proximity (230 m) and lack of concern about concentration or neighborhood character supports the viability of bars in this corridor.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Recent ABC Type 48 referral at 627 Grant Ave (78 m away), approved February 2025 for an existing restaurant and full bar (Far East Café) in the CVR district. Shows Planning's willingness to approve on-sale licenses on the Grant Avenue corridor very close to the subject site.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Agency referral: Planning approved a Type 48 continuation (existing use since 1965) at 627 Grant, one block from 555 Grant, in February 2025. The proximity and recent date confirm that the Grant Avenue corridor continues to support on-sale alcohol uses and that concentration is not a barrier.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: ABC Type 48 bar referral at 447 Bush Street, 230 m away, decided May 2016 for entertainment and arts use in the C-3-R district. Earlier approval at the same address as 2022-004266MIS, showing a long-standing bar location near the subject site.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Agency referral: Planning approved a Type 48 bar at 447 Bush in 2016 in the C-3-R district as permitted under Sections 210.2 and 102. The location has held a bar license continuously, demonstrating stable bar operations close to the Chinatown boundary without neighborhood conflict.

filing_playbook.action: Confirm formula retail status and floor area with Planning before filing the CUA application.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Contact SF Planning's information counter or submit a Preliminary Project Assessment (PPA) request stating the business name, whether it is part of a chain with other locations sharing the name or look, and the floor area of the bar space in square feet. Planning will confirm whether formula retail review (Planning Code Section 303(i)) or the 2,500 sq ft use-size trigger (Section 810) applies. If either applies, the CUA application must address those criteria; if not, the CUA is solely for the bar use. Budget 2–4 weeks for a PPA response or ask at the counter if the answers are straightforward.

filing_playbook.action: Obtain Planning Commission approval of the CUA at the public hearing.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: At the Commission hearing, present the operations plan and respond to any public comment. Emphasize the business's fit with the neighborhood (Chinatown visitor and arts corridor), measures to manage noise and litter (community liaison, posted exit notices, daily sidewalk monitoring), and compliance with the conditions imposed at 690 Sacramento Street (2023). If the Commission approves the CUA. If the Commission continues the hearing for revisions, address the requested changes and return for approval.
filing_playbook.verification_note: Cut down to the part the cited record states.

timeline_cost.notes: The day range (120–300 days) and cost range ($4,155–$18,250 in government fees) are the time and cost to obtain the three approvals in the entitlement path when they are granted: Conditional Use Authorization (120–300 days, $3,100–$15,000 per the catalog, depending on construction cost and fee waiver eligibility), Health permit to operate (14–45 days to issue after application, $470 application fee in 2026–27, included in the building permit timeline), and Building permit with change of use (14–120 days for plan check and issuance, $800–$15,000 depending on construction valuation, per the catalog). The timeline assumes the CUA is approved at the first hearing and no appeal is filed (add 1–2 months if appealed), that building plans are complete and pass review without major revisions (incomplete plans can add 2–4 months), and that the ABC Type 42 application and PCN finding (if required) proceed in parallel with construction (60–150 days per the catalog, with $1,000–$1,600 in ABC fees not included in this range because the alcohol row status is insufficient information and the ABC license is not in the entitlement path). The cost range includes only the Planning CUA fee, the building permit fee, the health permit application fee, and the SF business registration fee ($55–$700); it does not include architect fees, construction costs, ABC license fees, state business registration ($70–$150), or ongoing costs such as insurance and payroll taxes. If the CUA is denied or the building permit uncovers a code issue that cannot be resolved, the timeline and cost figures do not apply. Confirm the current CUA and building permit fee schedules with Planning and DBI, as fees are adjusted annually for CPI and by construction valuation.

status_definitions.allowed: Allowed: the cited records or code sections show this approval is available as of right, or already exists for this space, without a discretionary hearing.
status_definitions.further_review: Further review: the approval is obtainable only through a discretionary or multi-step review (a hearing, a referral, a licence investigation) whose result the records do not settle.
status_definitions.potential_blocker: Potential blocker: a cited rule, cap or record could stop this approval or force a change to the concept unless a specific condition is met.
status_definitions.not_permitted: Not permitted: a cited code section prohibits this use or approval at this address as the concept is described.
status_definitions.insufficient_information: Insufficient information: the records in hand do not show whether this approval is needed or obtainable; the could-not-establish section says what would settle it.

confidence_definitions.verified: Verified: stated directly by a cited record or code section that applies to this exact address, parcel or zoning district.
confidence_definitions.likely_applicable: Likely applicable: inferred from cited records of comparable cases or from a general rule; not stated for this address.
confidence_definitions.needs_confirmation: Needs confirmation: plausible but not supported by a record in hand; confirm with the agency or document named.
confidence_definitions.professional_review_required: Professional review required: depends on plans, an inspection, or legal or design judgment that public records cannot supply.

records_summary: 555 Grant Ave is in the Chinatown Community Business (CCB) zoning district, where a Bar use is a conditional use requiring Planning Commission approval. The address currently holds off-sale ABC licenses (Type 20 and Type 86) for "Blue Stream Gallery and Gifts," a retail art gallery and liquor store approved by Planning in April 2023. The proposed transition from retail to an on-premises beer-and-wine bar (Type 42) is a change of use that will require a Conditional Use Authorization. Within 1,000 feet there is only one dated use decision in the last decade—not enough to establish a meaningful approval rate. Within 500 feet there are 3 active on-sale licenses and 13 registered food/drink businesses, suggesting moderate but not excessive concentration.
data_gaps: No hearing transcripts or decision memoranda extracted for the 690 Sacramento CUA (2023-005339CUA), so the reasons for the approval conditions are not shown.
The ABC license database does not expose detailed conditions or operating restrictions for the nearby on-sale licenses.
No census tract undue-concentration determination is included; ABC will evaluate this separately during the Type 42 application.
The withdrawn CUA at 717 California (2019-021010CUA) gives no reason for the withdrawal in the record.
Registered business data (within 500 ft) does not distinguish currently operating establishments from closed ones; the count of 13 food/drink businesses may include inactive registrations.
No Planning Code history before 2022 is loaded, so earlier changes to CCB rules for bars are not shown.
